0.0.n: A casual transition introducing what the speaker will do next.

0.1.n: The plain form of 寝る comes before 前 to describe an action that has not happened yet.

0.2.n: After a plain-form verb, 前 places something earlier than that action.

0.3.n: に marks 寝る前 as the time when the alarm will be set.

0.4.n: A borrowed word written in katakana, used here with かける.

0.5.n: を marks アラーム as the thing being set.

0.6.n: Polite form of かける; with アラーム, it describes setting an alarm.

0.8.n: The speaker repeats the noun alone for emphasis.

1.0.n: A time word made the topic by は.

1.1.n: は marks 明日 as the topic: the speaker is discussing tomorrow's plan.

1.2.n: 時 after a number indicates the hour.

1.3.n: に marks the specific time the speaker wants to wake up.

1.4.n: 起きる becomes 起きたい by replacing る with たい to express the speaker's desire.

1.5.n: ので gives a reason and links it to the alarm-setting plan that follows.

2.0.n: 半 after the hour means thirty minutes past it.

2.1.n: と links this alarm time to the next one in the list.

2.3.n: 時 marks the hour; the following 45分 adds the minutes.

2.4.n: 分 marks minutes, completing 7時45分 as 7:45.

2.5.n: と continues the list by connecting this time to the next.

2.7.n: 時 marks the hour; the following 50分 adds the minutes.

2.8.n: 分 marks minutes, completing 7時50分 as 7:50.

2.10.n: そして introduces the final alarm time after the preceding list.

2.11.n: This is the last of the four listed alarm times.

2.12.n: に marks the listed times as when the alarms should go off.

2.13.n: Japanese nouns do not need a plural ending; the four times show that multiple alarms are meant.

2.14.n: を marks アラーム as what the speaker will set.

2.15.n: Polite form of かける, used for a planned action here.

3.0.n: そう confirms or reaffirms what the speaker has just said.

3.2.n: The noun is repeated alone, with the rest of the thought left understood.

0.lit: Then, before sleeping, I will set an alarm. Alarm.
0.tip: Use a plain-form verb + 前に to say before doing something.

1.lit: As for tomorrow, because I want to wake up at eight,
1.tip: ので introduces the reason for the action in the next line.

2.lit: For seven thirty, and seven forty-five, and seven fifty, and then eight, I will set alarms.
2.tip: One に after the final time can mark the whole list of alarm times.

3.tip: そう can stand alone as a brief confirmation meaning that's right.
